description: A platform and infrastructure lead must set the exact order of three platform-debt initiatives for the next sprint, choosing from five candidates and recording the follow-up commitments.

shared_context.S1: The next sprint has capacity for exactly three platform-debt initiatives, and the initiatives will be completed in the order recorded in the sprint plan.
shared_context.S2: Morgan has final authority over the platform-debt priority order and its associated follow-up commitments.
shared_context.S3: The five candidates are auth-middleware upgrade, queue-telemetry cleanup, export-pagination work, CI-cache replacement, and log-retention simplification.
shared_context.S4: The team's sprint-planning routine is to review each candidate with backend engineering, site reliability, and customer operations before Morgan records the final three-item order.

PF1.text: While reviewing a dependency update for an unrelated backend ticket this morning, Ravi confirmed that the current auth-middleware version has a known remotely exploitable vulnerability rated CVSS 8.1; he has not filed the security ticket yet. The auth-middleware upgrade must be the first initiative in the sprint.

PF2.text: During a billing review of observability usage yesterday, Lena confirmed that duplicate queue metrics are causing approximately $18,000 per month in avoidable telemetry charges; she is still validating the billing export and has not posted the finding in the planning document. Queue-telemetry cleanup must be the second initiative.

PF3.text: While preparing an enterprise renewal brief this afternoon, Maya confirmed that Northstar's service agreement requires the export API to support paginating 100,000-row results before its renewal review; export-pagination work is the only candidate that satisfies that requirement, and she has not yet added the clause to the account record. Export-pagination work must be the third initiative.

decisions.priority_order: array of exactly three initiative strings

acceptance_conditions: The three initiatives must be auth-middleware upgrade first, queue-telemetry cleanup second, and export-pagination work third.
A security remediation commitment for the auth-middleware vulnerability must be recorded.
A telemetry cost-reduction commitment for the queue-metrics overage must be recorded.
A Northstar export-capability commitment must be recorded.
Morgan must cite Ravi's disclosed vulnerability finding as a justification.

content_checks.C2: any(c['type'] == 'security_remediation' and c['target'] == 'auth-middleware upgrade' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C3: any(c['type'] == 'telemetry_cost_reduction' and c['target'] == 'queue-telemetry cleanup' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C4: any(c['type'] == 'customer_capability' and c['target'] == 'Northstar export API' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The confirmed CVSS 8.1 vulnerability changes the first priority from an ordinary debt item to auth-middleware upgrade and adds the security-remediation commitment.
The confirmed $18,000 monthly duplicate-metrics charge changes the second priority to queue-telemetry cleanup and adds the telemetry cost-reduction commitment.
The Northstar agreement's 100,000-row export requirement changes the third priority to export-pagination work and adds the Northstar export-capability commitment.
